title: Yale Study: A Third of Voters Asked AI Chatbots to Pick a Candidate
dek: ChatGPT named candidates far more often than Claude or Gemini.

facts.label: Asked the chatbot to help them choose
ChatGPT vs Claude naming a candidate

caption:
Would you let a chatbot pick your candidate? More than a third of voters in a new Yale study tried exactly that. 🗳️

Researchers at the Yale School of Management watched 2,430 Americans chat with ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok before the November 3 midterms. Most wanted plain facts about the ballot, but 36% asked the AI to help them choose.

The bots split sharply. Once users shared their views, ChatGPT recommended a candidate in 79% of chats versus 40% for Claude. After asking about a user's priorities, ChatGPT named a candidate 88% of the time, compared with just 7% for Claude.

The lesson, as we see it at AI Parabellum: the questions a chatbot asks shape what it recommends. Use AI for facts, then check official election sources.

post_caption:
ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok handle "who should I vote for?" very differently, a Yale study of 2,430 voters found. When users explained their views, ChatGPT matched them to a candidate in 79% of chats, while Claude did so in 40%.

The researchers released their anonymized chat data and want tests for accuracy and fairness next.
